The study encompasses a meticulous data collection process, preprocessing steps, the selection of the DenseNet121 model architecture, model training, and evaluation of the model's performance through a range of metrics, including accuracy (93.42), precision, recall, and the Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC). To enhance the transparency and interpretability of the model, employed the Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) technique, enabling to visualize the regions within images that influenced the model's decision-making. The research provides valuable insights into the development and evaluation of AI systems for image identification, particularly in the context of distinguishing between real and fake content. Furthermore, the interpretability techniques shed light on the model's decision-making process. This research contributes to the field of image authentication and paves the way for enhanced image classification in the era of synthetic media.

articleTitle: Tomato Leaf Disease Detection: Deciphering Disease Severity with CNN-RF Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive methodological approach to classify the severity level of tomato leaf disease, ranging from mild (1–10%) to severe (91–100%). Consequently, the study aims to develop a hybrid model of CNN for feature extraction that is insensitive to subtle variations in the illness effect and RF as a classification engine, which leads to excessive label noise levels, giving superior performance with smaller training sets. The data set, extended with various signs reflecting the disease manifestation, was processed using multi-layer CNN. Then, it was classified into ten severity levels using an RF model. The model's performance was highly evaluated, and the results were found to have accuracy values ranging from 91.21% to 94.57%, a recall value between, and an F-Score in the range of %. The figures show great accuracy in terms of prediction by the model, which is an idea that fits into several categories but at a high point. The confusion matrix gives a much clearer picture of the model's performance, with most predictions being accurate along that diagonal. Still, occasionally, there are cases when one class or another gets confused. A macro average F1 score showed 92.67% for the model, demonstrating consistency in performance above class zero but no bias towards support (negative value). Considering the unbalanced number of courses, however, there was a slight increase to 92.70%. Since most classes are more numerous, these exercises have marginally increased performance. The overall micro-average was 92.70%, signaling the average model's correctness and consistency with every aspect combined. Though the visible strengths were evident, total accuracy was formulated at 81.98%, which shows lowering different elements of the applied model more defensively until higher preference. In conclusion, the combination of CNN and RF creates a basis for hope in precision agriculture, providing an informative tool to aid disease control through their detailed nature, thus painting them as essential tools for sustainability. There is also a possibility that machine learning methods can be used.

articleTitle: Cached-N-Proxy: An Intelligent Proxy Algorithm for Preventing Insider Email Threats to Mail Servers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Insider threats are serious security risks that come from people who work for or are contracted by an organization, such as partners, employees, or contractors. These people use their authorized access to commit hostile acts against the infrastructure, data, or assets of the company. Serious ramifications could result from these dangers, such as financial losses, reputational harm, data breaches, and possible threats to national security. Enterprises must strengthen their defenses with strong intrusion detection and prevention systems because of the growing attack surface for insider threats caused by the increasing adoption of digital technology and remote work habits. Organizations must use a combination of preventive strategies and detection mechanisms, such as privileged access management (PAM), role-based access control, data loss prevention (DLP) techniques, two-factor authentication, and thorough insider threat awareness training, to effectively combat insider threats.

articleTitle: Enhancing Diagnostic Accuracy in Medical Imaging: Integrating GAN-Based Data Augmentation for Balanced Dataset Creation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Advancements in medical imaging have been substantially driven by deep learning technologies, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). A critical hurdle in this domain is the imbalance of datasets, where certain medical conditions are underrepresented, leading to potential biases in diagnostic models. This research addresses the imbalance in medical imaging datasets, specifically in chest radiography, by leveraging Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for data augmentation. The study utilizes the ChestXray2017 dataset, which is skewed towards pneumonia cases, resulting in a dearth of normal chest X-ray images. To counter this, Deep Convolution Generative Adversarial Networks (DCGAN) were employed to generate synthetic images of normal chest X-rays, thus aiming to balance the dataset. In this study, we conducted a comparative analysis of a Convolutional Neural Network's (CNN) performance on a chest radiography dataset, before and after augmenting it with Deep Convolution Generative Adversarial Network (DCGAN)-generated images. Initially, the CNN trained on the un-augmented dataset achieved 93% training accuracy and 87% validation accuracy. After integrating 400 synthetic normal chest X-ray images, the training accuracy slightly increased to 95%, while the validation accuracy notably improved to 89%. This enhancement in validation accuracy demonstrates the model's improved generalization capabilities due to a more balanced training dataset. Our results indicate that GAN-based data augmentation effectively addresses class imbalances in medical imaging datasets, potentially leading to more accurate and reliable diagnostic models. However, the study also underscores the need for further research into the quality and ethical implications of using synthetic images in medical diagnostics. Overall, the integration of GAN-generated images into CNN training presents a promising method for improving classification performance in medical imaging, offering a practical approach to overcome challenges associated with data scarcity and imbalance.

articleTitle: Handwritten English Script Recognition System Using CNN and LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: In this digital era, computers and phones are more important than ever, but many people still prefer handwritten documents to digital formats. Sometimes, storing, carrying, and reading through all handwritten documents at once is difficult, so there is a need to convert handwritten documents into digital versions. This paper presents two classification algorithms to convert into digital form: one is classifying words directly using CNN, and the other is character segmentation. The proposed model is based on a convolutional neural network, which was trained using word images from the IAM dataset. The number of layers and dataset size are kept smaller so that training and testing can be done on the CPU instead of the GPU. The proposed model consists of CNN layers for character recognition and LSTM layers for word and syntax correction. The recognition system takes an image as input and displays the digital version of a handwritten document as output after recognition. The CTC loss function and CTC decoder were used after LSTM to align sequences. This paper covers detailed intuition about the architecture and implementation of the proposed system, and its performance was evaluated based on the correct prediction of characters.

articleTitle: Deep Learning and Crow Search to Detect Skin Cancer in Dermoscopic Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: The accurate and timely diagnosis of skin cancer is crucial for reducing the associated mortality and morbidity rates, given the prevalence of this severe condition. Dermoscopic pictures provide doctors and researchers a closer look at skin lesions. This research uses cutting-edge image analysis and machine learning (ML) methods to provide a framework for dermatoscopic skin cancer analysis. We present the Crow Search Algorithm with Deep Learning for Skin Cancer Diagnoses on Dermoscopy Images (CSADL-SCDDI) model in this study. Bilateral filter (BF) preprocessing improves dermatoscopic pictures in the model. This preprocessing phase prepares pictures for analysis. For feature extraction, SqueezeNet is used. SqueezeNet is ideal for extracting key visual information due to its small, efficient design. SqueezeNet extracts complete characteristics for reliable skin cancer diagnosis. Model categorization uses Recurrent Neural Networks. RNNs excel at sequential data processing and feature set temporal relationships. RNNs can track skin lesion evolution, making them ideal for identifying benign from malignant skin cancer. The Crow Search Algorithm (CSA) optimizes hyper-parameters to improve model performance. CSA is inspired by crows' sophisticated foraging and used to fine-tune RNN parameters. This enhancement boosts system diagnostic accuracy. The system is tested on a large dataset of dermatoscopic pictures to prove its effectiveness. The framework's robustness and reproducibility in skin cancer analysis suggest it might greatly enhance diagnostic techniques.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Recognition of Hand Written Telugu Characters: Natural Language Processing and Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Handwritten character recognition has wider application in many areas including heritage documents, education, document digitalization, language processing, and assisting the visually handicapped and other related areas. The paper tries to improve the accuracy and efficiency of recognizing handwritten letters of Telugu language scripts, a difficult task for computers. Telugu is most widely spoken language in southern part of India, it has rich cultural heritage. Using the Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK), this study investigates ways to enhance recognition accuracy by analyzing handwritten content and implementing methods such as feature extraction and classification. The purpose is to use NLTK's capabilities to develop handwritten character recognition.

articleTitle: A CNN-based Stutter Detection Using MFCC Features with Binary Cross-Entropy Loss Function
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Stuttering is a condition where people have difficulty speaking smoothly. This includes repeating certain sounds or phrases in their speech. Autism, on the other hand, is a condition that affects communication and social interactions, leading to challenges in expressive speech, social cues, and interpersonal engagement. Stuttering is not a psychological issue; it can <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{con}_{\gamma}$</tex> tribute to social anxiety and low self-esteem. Currently, there is no known cure for stuttering; however, it can be effectively treated using speech-based stimulation to improve fluency. This study introduces a approach to stutter detection using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC) feature extraction on the LibriStutter dataset. The research rigorously evaluates the performance of three loss functions binary cross-entropy, categorical cross-entropy, and log cosh highlighting their impact on CNN model accuracy. Notably, binary cross-entropy emerges as the most effective, achieving a remarkable testing accuracy of 86.32%. The study includes detailed insights into the methodology, specifically emphasizing the utilization of a 1D Convolutional Layer with 32 filters, max pooling layer (2), dropout layer (0.2), ReLu activation and other components in the CNN architecture. Additionally, the results underscore the superior performance optimization achieved by the binary cross-entropy loss function. This research not only advances stutter detection methodologies but also highlights the pivotal role of the chosen loss function in achieving superior accuracy.

articleTitle: Enhancing Social Media Sarcasm Detection Using Chicken Swarm Optimization and Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Understanding social media sarcasm is a difficult but crucial NLP issue. Machine learning (ML) algorithms are needed to effectively discern sarcastic undertones in text due to its contextual and linguistic complexity. Traditional ML models distinguish sarcasm from sincerity via sentiment analysis, context-specific variables, and language markers. As online communication evolves, more complex technologies are needed to understand language's subtleties. The merging of deep learning (DL) approaches with contextual embedding has greatly improved sarcasm detection systems, allowing them to analyze text more precisely and contextually. The CSOA-GNN model, which combines the Chicken Swarm Optimization Algorithm (CSOA) with Graph Neural Networks to identify sarcasm. After rigorous data pre-processing, the model embeds words using TF-IDF (Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency). Sarcasm's unique language traits are vectorized for ML analysis using this method. GNN is then used to classify. Its ability to map out and grasp the complicated network of contextual links and dependencies among words inside sentences improves the model's sarcasm detection accuracy. CSOA is crucial to optimizing GNN performance in this model. CSOA optimizes the GNN hyperparameters to match social media text's sarcastic expressions. This unique technique relies on GNN-based classification, CSOA-based parameter optimization, and TF-IDF word embeddings, which provide encouraging results that demonstrate their efficacy. As they increase social media sarcasm detection accuracy and advance NLP. This study introduces the CSOA-GNN paradigm, enabling more advanced, contextually aware, and nuanced language interpretation systems. It advances our understanding of the complicated world of online communication, where sarcasm, frequently laced with nuanced indications and contextual richness, is a constant challenge. This model shows that powerful optimization methods may be integrated with neural network topologies, enabling new research and development opportunities for more refined and intelligent NLP systems.

articleTitle: Optimizing Underwater IoT Routing with Multi-Criteria Decision Making and Uncertainty Weights
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Effective data routing is vital in the Internet of Things (IoT) paradigm, especially in underwater mobile sensor networks where inefficiency can lead to significant resource consumption. This article presents an innovative method designed to enhance network performance and reduce resource usage, while also accurately determining component weights in these networks, ensuring quality service. Building upon previous re-search on multi-criteria decision-making systems in coastal RPL networks, our method involves key adaptations for underwater environments. It integrates comprehensive network features to identify the optimal parent node for each sensor, employing the fuzzy SWARA decision-making approach under uncertain conditions. This method takes into account various factors including hops, energy, ARSSI rate, delay, ETX, link delivery rate, and depth to determine the most effective parent node assignment. Through simulation, our approach demonstrates marked improvements in network performance compared to existing solutions. These advancements are significant, offering a new direction in enhancing underwater IoT communications and suggesting wider applications for IoT systems facing similar challenges.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Enabled Classification of Microscopic Blood Samples for Leukemia Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: White blood cell (WBC) cancer, or leukemia, harms the body's bone marrow and blood. If not detected at an early stage, the illness may be fatal. When clinically significant features and biologically explicable methods are employed to determine the severity of the disease and identify malignancy, machine-controlled identification of cancerous cells from microscopic diagnostic assay images of blood samples helps alleviate leukemia's diagnostic issues and yields better results. This proposed method used deep learning CNN model YOLOv5s which is fast and lightweight. This paper achieved a Metric precision of 94% and a mean average precision (mAP@0.5) of 98%.

articleTitle: Enhancing IoT Container Scheduling in the Cloud with Multi-Objective Accelerated PSO
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Containers are encapsulated bundle of application and its dependent libraries made to execute in the operating system without the need of pre-configurations. Containers need to be scheduled effectively to leverage the full potential of underlying physical infrastructure. The integration of contain- ers in IoT, facilitates streamlined deployment, scalability, and management of diverse applications, enhancing the efficiency and flexibility of Internet of Things ecosystems. In the realm of container scheduling, the Multi-Objective Accelerated Particle Swarm Optimization (MOAPSO) algorithm emerges as a more effective solution compared to the standard Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm, particularly when tasked with scheduling a substantial number of containers. Its scalability proves to be a standout feature, positioning MOAPSO as a versatile tool capable of efficiently scheduling in Internet of Things (IoT) applications within expansive cloud environments. The traditional PSO algorithm, while a benchmark, achieves an accuracy rate of 80%, but the introduction of the Accelerated Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm elevates this metric to an impressive 90.7%. This underscores the enhanced performance and accuracy achievable through the accelerated variant, show- casing its potential to significantly impact container scheduling, particularly in the context of large-scale cloud deployments and IoT applications. This means that the proposed method is able to schedule the containers for IoT applications more efficiently, reduce the computational time, consume less energy, emit less CO2 and heat, and utilize cloud resources more effectively.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Security Enhancements in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Wireless sensor networks have garnered significant adoption as a technology for collecting and analyzing data from the environment. Their versatility and wide-ranging applications, encompassing critical military operations, forest fire detection, healthcare systems, and civilian uses, have made them a focal point of extensive research. The potential of WSNs to provide valuable insights and address various real-world challenges has spurred significant interest and exploration in the scientific community. Nevertheless, Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are susceptible to security threats, especially in unattended environments. To address these threats, the popular Low-Energy Adaptive Clustering Hierarchy protocol is deployed with machine learning techniques. This paper makes an analysis of different machine learning algorithms with multiple class of parameters and evaluates it with criterion as such favorable for a WSN. The Random Forest technique, which allows for the classification of assaults such as blackhole attacks, grayhole attacks, TDMA attacks, and flooding attacks, is the most suitable algorithm for intrusion detection. It comprises six extracted characteristics. The accuracy score is 99.12% with prediction accuracy for attacks: 87%, 89%, 92% and 93% respectively. Unlike detecting the anomaly alone, this mechanism when given to a centralized management system become a smart governance model. This prevents the network from different intrusion methodologies and enhance the characteristics such as energy efficiency, network lifetime, throughput, performance and security issue of the wireless sensor network.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Impact of HRM Algorithms on Employee Morale in Multinational Corporations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: This paper offers a complete analysis of the effect of human resources management (HRM) algorithms on employee morale in multinational groups. To this quit, the study uses worker rankings and critiques of the effectiveness of HRM algorithms employed at multinational corporations. Facts accumulated from the corporations include worker surveys, attention corporations, and interviews. The findings showed that HRM algorithms had a full-size impact on employee morale, with excellent correlations of more significant than zero. Six among algorithm usage and suggested morale. Similarly, analysis found that the impact of HRM algorithmic techniques strongly relied on the nature and timing of the HRM set of rules' implementation, as well as corporation size and type. Businesses with larger organizational sizes generally had a larger pronounced impact from HRM algorithms on worker morale. The findings of this observation offer precious insights into how HRM can satisfactory rent algorithmic strategies to enhance employee morale in giant firms.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease in Respiratory Audio Signals Using CNN and LSTM Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) ranks third globally in terms of cause of death, after heart disease and cancer. Persistent lung conditions that obstruct airflow from the lungs can lead to difficulty in breathing. Symptoms of COPD encompass coughing, chest tightness, shortness of breath, and wheezing. While there is presently no recognized cure for COPD, medications are available to manage symptoms and hinder the progression of the disease. According to the Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD), the four stages of COPD are mild, moderate, severe, and very severe. Deep learning models such as Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) were utilized to identify COPD from respiratory audio data. The Respiratory Sound Database dataset was gathered via Kaggle. To identify COPD, the CNN and LSTM models are used independently. With the LSTM model achieving 98.2% accuracy and the CNN model achieving 92.3% accuracy, the findings show that the trained models obtained great precision. Life expectancy can be extended and quality of life enhanced by early identification and treatment of COPD. It can lessen exacerbations, increase survival, stop or slow the disease's course, and save money.

Author Keywords: Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD)

articleTitle: Lightweight Symmetric Key Encryption to Improve the Efficiency and Safety of the IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: IoT is a potential future technology that will link billions of things. In IoT applications, security is crucial, yet several encryption rounds might waste device resources and energy. A more simplified approach is needed here. One alternative is to use a simpler encryption technique that balances security and computing performance. A 64-bit block cypher requires a 64-bit key for data encryption. This technique uses Feistel cypher and uniform substitution to substitute network simulation, assuring strong encryption. This technique delivers significant security with only five rounds of encryption, according to research. The proposed work implements a symmetric key lightweight technique for secure picture and text transfer. To protect data, the system uses picture encryption and reversible data concealment. This study has various benefits over previous algorithms. First, it computes quicker, making it ideal for resource-constrained IoT devices. The algorithm's simplicity boosts energy efficiency and device performance. Lastly, its greater Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) indicates better picture quality retention during encryption and transmission. Symmetric key cryptography works for many picture formats. An appealing graphical user interface has been created for a real-time picture capture system. This comprehensive approach assures that the algorithm fulfils IoT application security criteria and improves usability and practicality, creating a safer and more efficient IoT environment.

articleTitle: Intelligent Surveillance and Protection System for Farmlands from Animals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Agriculture is an important area for growing crops, as food is the main source of sustainability. India, with its vast agricultural area, has a wide variety of crops, from food grains to vegetables. However, few crops are destroyed by animal attacks, so a proper monitoring system is needed to protect the crops from animals. Crops are mainly damaged by animals such as buffalo, cattle, goats, birds, and wild elephants. This causes huge losses to farmers. The farmer cannot protect the crops if animals stay in the field for more than 24 hours. To address this issue, an animal detection system that detects the presence of animals has been developed. It provides the warning and redirects animals without harming them by using Machine learning and Image processing technique. The proposed system is deployed in the fields with a camera which continuously monitors. When an animal enters the field, it receives a short urge, which only threatens the animal to leave the field but doesn't harm the animal by using a laser beam instead of a fence that can harm the animal. In addition, the animal is redirected by playing sound of certain frequency and the same is intimated through SMS for quick notification to farmer. Light-dependent resistance sensors (LDRs) are often used for distance measurement. This system is also excellent at detection of various obstacles (wood, plastic, mirrors, plywood, concrete, etc.). The minimum obstacle size that the system can detect is about 5cmx5cm. The proposed developed model is a lab scale and can be scaled for further use. The overall safety of the crop was ensured from the animals by this system and thus protects the losses that occurred to farmers. To detect and monitor the movements of animals the developed system uses laser beam. Further, this model ensures the complete safety of the crop from the animals and prevents the loss of the farmer.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms on Parkinson's Disease Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive loss of motor control, resulting in tremors and severe difficulties in speech and face mobility. In the absence of traditional methods to detect PD in its early stage, there is a need for the present medical fraternity to rely on Machine learning-based solutions, considering numerous physical factors to deduce near-accurate assessments and personalized care plans. This research work proposes eight distinct methods to analyse the performance of nine State-Of-The-Art supervised Machine Learning (ML) algorithms using 195 voice samples of patients. Among the eight methods proposed, the method involving the classification of data based on the target variable and subsequent pre-processing using Log transformation and Robust Scaler, showcased unparalleled performance achieving an ideal F1 score.

articleTitle: Combining Deep Learning Techniques for Enhanced Human Activity Recognition: A Hybrid CNN-LSTM Fusion Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Over recent years conventional pattern recognition pattern recognition techniques have advanced significantly. Nonetheless, these methods heavily depend on manual feature extraction, potentially limiting the overall performance and generalizability of the model. Given the rising prominence and efficiency of deep learning approaches, there has been a growing interest in leveraging these methods for human action recognition in mobile and wearable computing contexts. Despite this enthusiasm, existing deep learning architectures may not fully capitalize on the complex spatio-temprial patterns inherent in human actions. Moreover, deploying deep learning models in real-world scenarios often demands robustness, efficiency, and interpretability, which remain significant challenges. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel approach: a deep neural network that integrates convolutional layers with long short-term memory(LSTM) units. By fusing the strengths of CNNs in spatial feature extraction with the temporal modelling capabilities of LSTMs, our hybrid architecture aims to enhance the accuracy and robustness of human activity recognition systems. This fusion enables the model to automatically learn hierarchical representations from data, eliminating the need for manual feature engineering. The approach holds, eliminating the need for manual feature engineering. The approach holds promise for applications in healthcare, sports analysis and assistive technology, where accurate and reliable HAR is essential. Overall, The proposed model achieves accuracy of 80% and 92% on the UCF50 dataset, a comprehensive video dataset, utilizing the CNN and LSTM models individually, respectively. These findings indicate that our hybrid model exhibits superior robustness and enhanced activity detection capabilities compared to certain previously reported results of only sensor data, surpassing an 90% accuracy threshold when trained on video-based data. Notably, the model demonstrates adaptability in extracting activity features whie maintaining a streamlined parameter count and achieving heightened.

articleTitle: Infant Cry Classification using CNN-MFCC Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Classifying infant cries is crucial to correctly identifying a newborn's needs or health concerns. This paper presents a novel approach that uses Mel-Frequency Cepstral Co-efficients (MFCCs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to automatically classify baby cries. Effective cry signal en-coding is accomplished by utilizing MFCC features to capture distinctive acoustic qualities. CNN architecture is used to process these features, allowing for the accurate classification of baby cries into categories like hunger, discomfort, pain, and tiredness. The model's performance on a variety of datasets demonstrates its potential for early identification of health issues or specific needs in newborns. Furthermore,The mathematical outcomes of the conclusion indicate that the CNN model's accuracy was 94%, which was marginally lower than the 96% accuracy of the Decision Tree model.. In spite of this, the CNN is a better choice due to its strong generalization, ability to control class imbalance, and potential for overfitting. By merging CNN and MFCC, this method provides a dependable and adaptable means of automatically interpreting infant cries, advancing the field of technology-assisted healthcare applications for early childhood development.

articleTitle: Lung Nodule Segmentation in CT Scans Using 3D U-Net Models with Inception and ResNet Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Lung cancer is a significant contributor to global cancer-related fatalities. Utilizing deep learning techniques has the potential to enhance the detection rate of lung nodules in chest computed tomography (CT) scans, facilitating effective diagnosis and treatment planning. Moreover, given the three-dimensional (3D) nature of thoracic CT scans, 3D CNNs can effectively capture volumetric information embedded in the images. This study explores lung nodule segmentation using various 3D U-Net architectures: Standard 3D U-Net (Model-I), ResNet 3D U-Net (Model-II), Inception 3D U-Net (Model-III), and Inception-ResNet 3D U-Net (Model-IV); optimized with a combination of Dice and Focal Loss. These models were evaluated on an L1-patient test dataset. Model-II outperforms all the models, achieving an average dice similarity coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(DSC_{avg})$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.84\pm 0.06$</tex> and an average Jaccard index <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(IoU_{avg})$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.73\pm 0.09$</tex> on the test dataset. Moreover, this study identifies compromised predictions generated by the models and their associated characteristics. Addressing the issues with superior approaches is a crucial aspect to be considered in future work.

articleTitle: Dynamic Pricing: Trends, Challenges and New Frontiers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Modern dynamic pricing has emerged as a computer-automated strategy that has revolutionized pricing methodologies and consumer interactions across various industries. This paper delves into the intricate domain of dynamic pricing, presenting an overview of its significance and the complex factors influencing its implementation. Within the realms of computer science, this subject involves heuristic development, data science, and the design of robust system architectures. The paper extensively examines the application of dynamic pricing in critical sectors such as e-commerce, travel, energy, electric vehicle charging, cloud computing, and ride-sharing services. It highlights the strategies and algorithms employed in each sector, showcasing their effectiveness in adapting to dynamic market conditions. The pivotal role of competitive forces, demand dynamics, inventory management, and price discrimination in shaping dynamic pricing strategies is explored in depth. Furthermore, this paper identifies promising avenues for future research in dynamic pricing, spanning industries such as transportation, energy, online platforms, industrial parks, automated machine learning, emerging technologies, and real-time pricing. It serves as a comprehensive guide to the contemporary state-of-the-art in dynamic pricing, shedding light on its multifaceted nature, broad applications, and exciting prospects for advancement across diverse industries.

articleTitle: Interpretable Predictions for Crime Categories Using Log Loss Approach for Imbalanced Target Feature
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Crime indicates activities that infringe laws and regulations constituted by a governing authority. These wrongdoings can range from minor aberrations such as petty theft to more serious crimes like assault, robbery, or murder. Understanding crime patterns, causes, and trends is important for creating effective law enforcement strategies and enforcing policies that facilitate to a risk-free and stable society. This paper explores the interpretability of crime category predictions generated by XGBoost and Random Forest models on San Francisco crime data ranging 12 years. Notably, in comparison to other models, such as k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Stochastic Gradient Descent(SGD) and Naïve Bayes, our XGBoost and Random Forest models featured superior predictive excellence, Obtaining competitive log-loss scores of 2.277761 and 2.283956, respectively, to augment interpretability we have employed Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to clarify the decision-making processes of these models. This interpretability analysis would definitely add a deeper insight into the contributing factors of model's predictive behavior towards crime rate prediction. Additionally, we have dealt with imbalanced target feature as well. In comparison to existing research in the field, our work stands out by introducing advanced interpretability techniques, LIME and SHAP, enhancing transparency in crime prediction models. This innovative approach surpasses traditional methods, providing a more comprehensive understanding of crime dynamics and achieving superior predictive excellence. Innovation is introduced through the incorporation of advanced interpretability techniques, specifically Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP).

articleTitle: Epileptic Seizure Classification- A Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Recurrent seizures are a feature of epileptic seizure disorder, a brain ailment. An aberrant brain activity known as a seizure frequently causes changes in sensations, movements, or consciousness. Modified Convolutional Neural Networks (i.e. Feedforward Neural Network) is the deep learning technique utilized for seizure detection and classification, consisting of batch normalization, dense layer with ReLU activation function and a dropout layer. Due to the model's flexible architecture, it captures complex patterns in the EEG signals and the presence of dropout layer helps preventing the overfitting, batch normalization helps in stable and accelerated training, however of its high accuracy, the model may have memorized the data rather than learning the patterns, which could lead to poor performance on a new dataset. The model's output indicates a Testing classification accuracy of 98%, with validation accuracy of 97% and a validation loss of 3.89%.

articleTitle: English to Hindi Translation System Using Hybrid Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Good communication is critical for overcoming cultural and linguistic divides in today's internationalized society. An essential communication component is the Translation of written materials, primarily academic papers, from one language into another. This abstract focuses on the research involved in translating academic publications from Hindi to English. Translating Hindi academic papers into English is naturally hard due to the significant linguistic and cultural differences between the two languages. The proposed work provided an analytical analysis of various models used in language translation, including the seq-to-seq model, MT5, and LSTM, with the help of BLEU score, Learning rate, and average loss. MT5 model outshines others in terms of an average loss of 4.75; meanwhile, LSTM has an average loss of 5.56, and the seq-to-seq model has an average loss of 6.09, implying weaker Translation.

articleTitle: A Repository based Criminal Identification - Evolution in Forensics using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Suspecting the criminal is a critical process during the early stages of the investigation at the crime scene. The forensic examiner should start the difficult process of thorough examination with the evidence collected from the crime location in order to imagine the circumstances leading up to the incident. A meticulously planned crime scene investigation with advancement technology is required here. Even though forensic science has made substantial progress, more investigation is needed to discover whether these advancements have any additional benefits for addressing criminal cases. By building and maintaining a database of criminals, the proposed model enables the police department to identify criminals using evidence gathered from crime scenes and a “matching mechanism” to match the evidence with the database details. Maintaining a digital database of the relevant criminals' information and offering a simple matching mechanism via soft computing techniques would help police officials to identify the proper criminals more quickly and effectively. The database should contain the data on the “face” information (used to access the identity) of the criminals. This database has a lot of potential that can be realized in order to help avoid crimes, deceit, and aid with surveillance, among other things. Our suggested model, “CrimeNet,” is comprised of two layers: an EfficientNetv2b0 layer and a Data Augmentation layer. This model identifies whether the given image matches with previous criminal record.

articleTitle: DMMQBIN: Design of an Efficient Triple Metaheuristic Model for QoS-Aware Blockchain deployments in IoV Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving Internet of Vehicles (IoV) environment, block chain technology has proven to have significant potential for enabling secure, trustworthy, and decentralized data transfers. Nevertheless, the conventional application of block chain in Internet of Vehicles (IoV) networks often encounters challenges such as notable mining latency, heightened energy usage, and compromised network performance metrics like packet delivery ratio and throughput. Furthermore, these issues are not adequately addressed by existing methods, highlighting the need for an efficient optimization model to maximize blockchain installations. This study presents a novel Triple Meta-heuristic Model for effectively optimizing Quality of Service (QoS)-aware block chain installations in Internet of Vehicles (IoV) networks. The proposed model integrates the meta-heuristic techniques of Firefly Optimizer (FO), Bat Inspired Optimisation (BIO), and Jellyfish Search Optimizer (JSO). Every technique is necessary to optimize specific aspects of blockchain implementation. To reduce the likelihood of double-spending and data manipulation, JSO is used to identify the optimal models for block encryption and hashing. JSO is renowned for its efficacy and ability to conduct worldwide searches. BIO is driven by bats' echolocation habit to calculate the optimal blockchain length for sidechain creation. This enhances data availability and lowers latency. Lastly, the FO-which is well-known for its capacity for global optimization-is employed to determine which miner nodes are best suited for block addition, hence enhancing the network's resilience and transactional speed. With a 9.5% reduction in mining latency, the empirical results demonstrate that the suggested architecture works better for IoV communications than existing block chain models.

articleTitle: Navigating Activity Cliffs with Neural Combinatorial Optimization: A Graph-Based Roadmap for Drug Discovery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: In the drug discovery field, Graph Edit Distance (GED) has emerged as a powerful tool for calculating Activity Cliff Analysis (ACA). ACA is a crucial tool in drug discovery that helps identify pairs of compounds with similar structure while demonstrating vastly different biological activities. However, traditional GED algorithms face limitations in handling large and intricate molecular graphs. This paper demonstrates a novel approach that utilizes Neural Combinatorial Optimization (NCO) to optimize the GED algorithm, enabling it to efficiently calculate GED values, enhancing its performance. This proposed NCO-based GED algorithm is applied to activity cliff analysis, where it successfully identifies pairs of compounds with similar structures but different biological activities. This NCO framework offers a promising avenue for optimizing various computational algorithms in drug discovery and other domains. By successfully implementing this NCO-based approach, ACA and its impact on drug discovery could be revolutionised leading to faster, more accurate activity cliff identification, and ultimately, the potential for the creation of life-saving drugs.

articleTitle: Enhancing Gastrointestinal Image Classification: A Fusion of CNN and Vision Trasformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: In order to meet the pressing demand for early diagnosis in healthcare, we proposed a unique hybrid architecture in this study that is intended for the categorization of gastrointestinal (GI) illnesses. With fewer trainable parameters, faster training times, and less storage needed for model weights, our suggested architecture prioritizes efficiency achieves an impressive 94% accuracy. To effectively diagnose GI disorders, this design combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with Transformers. The creation of this hybrid architecture, which boasts excellent accuracy in illness categorization, decreased storage requirements, and efficiency in training, is one of the research's accomplishments. Our proposed model demonstrates its flexibility for many uses, encouraging simple implementation and expandability. Extensive tests performed on a large dataset of endoscopic images highlight our hybrid architecture's better performance over current techniques. With this study, diagnostics for gastrointestinal diseases have advanced significantly, opening the door to future diagnostic systems that will be more precise and effective. The proposed architecture has outperformed the traditional pre-trained models both in classification accuracy and time to train the model with no weights.

articleTitle: From Pixels to Prognosis: A Deep Dive into Lung Cancer Subtype Classification using Transfer learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Current diagnostic procedures, such as imaging tests and biopsies, are time intensive and prone to human error. As a result, we employed deep learning to uncover patterns and identify lung cancer from histology pictures. We hypothesised that combining two separate methods (transfer learning and data augmentation) would increase the efficacy of lung cancer detection. The study's dataset consisted of histology images for Lung Cancer and was quite unbalanced, with very few photos containing tumours. We hypothesised that transfer learning, which employs existing knowledge for classification and detection, would be effective on such an imbalanced dataset. To boost our learning, we employed data augmentation to incorporate changes into the dataset. This can be accomplished by implementing Sequential Keras Model Layers. We then tested the efficacy of various convolutional neural network models on this job. We achieved an accuracy of 87.50% utilising the transfer learning model MobileNetV2 as the basis model and numerous geometric changes, beating the cutting-edge convolutional neural network-based technique. We then analysed the results and published them on a website that people can access at any time and from any location.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis for Therapy Chatbots: A Comparison of Supervised Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: The maj ority of people in the world presently suffer from mental illness, and many of them are not even aware of it. Mental health awareness is important, but fear and ignorance often prevent people from talking about their issues. This work investigates the incorporation of sentiment analysis into therapy chatbots by utilizing deep learning and machine learning techniques, acknowledging the significance of mental health. By enabling users to interact with chatbots in a conversational manner, these systems aim to revolutionize mental health support. We evaluate various supervised learning algorithms for sentiment analysis within therapy chatbots, emphasizing their practicality and effectiveness. Our study reveals the Random Forest (RF) algorithm as a standout performer, achieving an impressive accuracy rate of 87%. This comparative analysis offers insights into the potential of these algorithms to enhance mental health assistance and user engagement, contributing to the advancement of conversational AI in mental health care. In light of our findings, this research underscores the significance of employing sentiment analysis within therapy chatbots and provides valuable insights into the comparative performance of supervised learning approaches, aligning with the overarching goal of enhancing mental health support through innovative technological solutions.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligent Techniques for Disease Detection in Tomato
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: The identification of diseases that affect the leaves and fruits of tomato plants is an urgent concern for farmers and gardeners because of the potential for production losses and a decline in the quality of fruits and vegetables. Detection at an early stage is essential for taking quick control measures to prevent the spread of illness. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches have emerged as potential technologies for automating illness diagnosis in recent years. These techniques ensure that diagnoses are accurate and efficient. This article is a comprehensive evaluation of the uses of machine learning and deep learning in the detection of illnesses in tomato plants. The purpose of this study is to investigate the efficiency of these methods and how they might be used to diagnose illnesses that affect leaves and fruits. An overview of the most common illnesses that affect tomato plants is presented at the beginning of the survey, with an emphasis placed on the need of prompt intervention. After that, it provides an explanation of the ideas and methodology of machine learning and deep learning, so providing the framework for the applications of these techniques in illness detection. The objectives of this research are to examine current machine learning and deep learning approaches for the diagnosis of plant diseases, with a specific emphasis on deep learning, namely convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which demonstrate substantial performance in the detection of tomato diseases. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have the potential to automatically recognise hierarchical structures in raw picture data, which will help facilitate accurate illness categorization. In order to promote the implementation of new technologies for early and accurate tomato disease diagnosis, this survey report serves as a significant resource for researchers, practitioners, and stakeholders in the agricultural industry. As a result, crop management practices and agricultural output are improved.

articleTitle: Enhancing Legal Decision Making: WRIT Case Outcome Prediction with LegalBERT Embeddings and AdaBoost Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Legal decision-making, the process of determining the outcome of court cases, is a pivotal aspect of the justice system. It involves evaluating evidence, interpreting laws, and ensuring justice is served. However, this process is challenging due to the complexity of legal cases, varying interpretations of laws, and the potential for lengthy court proceedings. In addition to these reasons, India also has one of the world's lowest ratios of judges to population. For swift and efficient disposal of justice, it is important to fast-track this process as much as possible. A traditional solution to this problem would take a considerable amount of time to show any meaningful results considering the current backlog of cases and the rate at which new cases are being filed each day. In order to overcome these difficulties, we employ text embeddings from LLM's with statistical classifiers to effectively and precisely forecast the outcomes for writ petitions. Our approach delivers an accuracy of 54% and a F1-score of 0.42 with LegalBERT embedder and AdaBoost classifier.

articleTitle: Integrated Framework for Accurate Change Detection and Deforestation Identification in Satellite Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: The escalation of deforestation, particularly in the urban periphery, underscores the urgency for advanced frameworks in change detection. This research addresses this imperative by introducing a comprehensive solution for precise identification of deforestation and change detection in satellite imagery. Our proposed approach encompasses two key frameworks: one focused on change detection and the other on deforestation identification. A Modified U-Net for change detection, emphasizing pixel-wise alterations in satellite imagery. Simultaneously, a VGG Net model is employed to identify deforested areas, focusing on distinguishing relevant features. The Modified U-Net architecture leads with an exceptional 99.25% accuracy, excelling in detecting nuanced alterations, especially in urban landscapes. Integration of the VGG Net model further amplifies accuracy, achieving a commendable 91.87% in pinpointing deforested areas. This dual proficiency showcases our framework's adaptability, adeptly handling diverse environmental monitoring challenges. Emphasizing robustness and effectiveness, our framework emerges as a pivotal tool in remote sensing, making significant contributions to environmental conservation and land-use monitoring.

articleTitle: NFTGenesis - An NFT Generation and Authentication System with Market Intelligence Using Deep Learning Based Steganography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: This research paper proposes a novel approach of integrating traditional steganography techniques with modern deep learning methodology as a solution against prevailing cyber fraud in the blockchain space. Despite standard authentication measures in place, Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) are prone to data theft, replication, and misrepresentation of ownership. Hence, our work leverages deep learning infused with advanced crypto-steganography to add multi-layered authentication to these digital tokens. The research elaborates on multiple utilities relevant to NFTs such as their generation, verification, and price forecasting, while emphasizing mainly on authentication to provide a secure ecosystem. The research aims to delve into multiple methodologies that are integrated into a robust, comprehensive and a user-friendly NFT minting platform that works cohesively with the blockchain network. Hence, an extensive study is undertaken on the applications of deep learning in countering data theft in the NFT marketplaces.

articleTitle: Enhanced Alzheimer's Disease Classification: A Stacked Model Fusion with Brain MRI Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is still a major global health issue that requires sophisticated staging and classification techniques. This paper introduces a novel approach to AD categorization, employing a stacked network architecture and feature extractions from InceptionV3, EfficientNetB0, and MobileNet models. The primary objective is to address the challenge of imbalanced datasets while minimizing the risk of overfitting. The proposed method utilizes brain MRI scans, extracting features and incorporating a Global Average Pooling (GAP) layer to improve the identification of critical features that correspond to AD phases. Combining the retrieved features results in a single set that helps with stage discrimination, followed by finishing via a SoftMax classifier. Model evaluation and validation are essential steps in determining the ideal model to minimize the risk of overfitting. A comprehensive evaluation is ensured by cross-validation (CV) using a 3-fold technique, which shows that the suggested Stacked Model has a better accuracy of 94.58%, closely followed by EfficientNetB0 at 90.70%. Both InceptionV3 and MobileNet exhibit competitive results, with accuracy rates of 89.46% and 87.60%, respectively. By presenting a strong approach to AD classification, this study advances the field of early detection and staging of AD by demonstrating the effectiveness of the Stacked network in identifying complex features that are indicative of different stages of AD progression within brain MRI datasets.

articleTitle: Enhancing Industrial Equipment Reliability: Advanced Predictive Maintenance Strategies Using Data Analytics and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: In today's dynamic industrial landscape, optimizing machinery performance and minimizing downtime are paramount for sustained operational excellence. This paper presents advanced predictive maintenance strategies, with a focus on leveraging machine learning and data analytics to enhance the reliability and efficiency of industrial equipment. The study explores the key components of predictive maintenance, including data collection, condition monitoring, predictive models, failure prediction, optimized maintenance scheduling and the extension of equipment longevity. The paper discusses how predictive maintenance aligns with modern industrial paradigms. The study evaluated the performance of five popular forecasting models like Random Forest, Linear Regression, Exponential Smoothing, ARIMA, and LSTM, to estimate maintenance for industrial equipment. The effectiveness of each model was evaluated using a number of performance metrics. The percentage of the variation in the real data that the model can explain is shown by the R-squared number. The lowest MSE, RMSE, and greatest R-squared values indicate a model's accuracy. The study highlights practical implications across diverse industries, showcasing the transformative impact of predictive maintenance on minimizing unplanned downtime, reducing maintenance costs, and maximizing the lifespan of critical machinery. When it comes to predictive maintenance for industrial machinery, the LSTM model has been shown to be the most accurate and efficient model with the highest R-squared value, indicating a better fit and higher predictive ability. As technology continues to evolve, the paper discusses future directions, including the integration of artificial intelligence and advanced analytics, and emphasizes the importance of continuous improvement in refining predictive maintenance strategies for the evolving needs of industries worldwide.

articleTitle: Predictive Analytics in Oncology: A Comprehensive Study on Lung Cancer Risk Factors and Machine Learning Model Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Cancer still remains one of the most fatal diseases in this world. Early detection and diagnoses can easily enhance treatment outcomes and survival probability by a great level. This paper presents the leverage of advanced machine learning techniques for cancer risk prediction using which timely intervention can be enabled. A comprehensive cancer dataset of 11 features capturing demographics, lifestyle habits, family history etc. was used to train prediction models based on logistic regression, random forests and neural networks. Extensive evaluations demonstrate the superiority of the neural network with near perfect precision, recall and F1-scores. The sensitivity analysis brought some of the most influential risk factors forward. The predictive performance proved the potential of machine learning in preventive oncology with data-driven screening recommendations and personalized care. Future work should focus on integrating di-verse health data and testing model performance in real clinical research.

articleTitle: Image Reconstruction and Facial Feature Extraction for Criminal Identification Using Machine Intelligence (Epic Vision)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Criminal detection continues to face challenges when dealing with blurry, fragmented, or ambiguous visual information from surveillance sources. This paper is devoted to a sophisticated machine intelligence approach that attempts to address these issues. The main objective is to reconstruct and enhance the facial features and to carefully extract unique facial features. This approach is poised to provide more accurate and effective criminal detection methods. To achieve these goals, the project uses extensive facial datasets and state-of-the-art neural network models. By doing so, it seeks to change the way law enforcement agencies interpret and analyze physical evidence. The implemented system not only focuses on improving facial images but also ensures that vital facial landmarks are retained even under harsh conditions This modification of features a environmental image quality changes this is the main strength of the project, with real-world criminals -Promising to increase the efficiency of the investigation This study highlights the power of machine intelligence in law enforcement, and provides actionable insights that can reshape current practices His innovative facial reconstruction and feature extraction techniques are at the forefront of technological advances in this field. Moreover, the results of the project extend beyond the immediate context and have global significance. They have the potential to increase the efficiency and success of global security agencies and, ultimately, to help maintain public safety and preserve justice. This approach not only improves facial images but also ensures the retention of crucial facial landmarks, even in adverse conditions. By leveraging state-of-the-art machine intelligence, this project aims to significantly enhance criminal detection methods, offering tangible benefits to law enforcement agencies worldwide.

articleTitle: Identification of Gender from the Shortest Speech using Hybrid and Optimised Spectral Features using Machine Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Amidst the contemporary tapestry of technological progression, the realm of speech processing assumes a paramount position, its significance underscored across a myriad of applications. Notably, gender identification from speech data emerges as a salient focal point within this domain, serving as a beacon of innovation and challenge alike.. This task holds particular import in domains such as criminal justice, where swift identification of a speaker's gender from recorded conversations can significantly expedite investigative processes. Our study delves into this imperative, specifically targeting gender identification within the context of the Telugu language-a linguistically rich Dravidian language widely spoken in South India. Navigating this terrain requires the deployment of sophisticated statistical models, including the Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) and the Hidden Markov Model (HMM), tailored to discern gender nuances from Telugu speech samples. At the core of our methodology lies the development of a meticulously curated dataset, finely attuned to the linguistic intricacies of Telugu. Employing advanced feature extraction techniques such as Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), derivatives thereof, and Zero Crossing Rate (ZCR), this work endeavor to encapsulate the subtle nuances inherent in gender-specific speech patterns within Telugu. Furthermore, to enhance classification accuracy, we harness Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to distill feature sets while retaining discriminatory power. This work underscores the efficacy of our approach, showcasing tangible improvements in gender classification accuracy across both original and reduced feature sets. Through meticulous comparative analyses, this work elucidates the efficacy of diverse feature extraction methodologies, providing insights into optimal strategies for gender identification within Telugu speech datasets. In essence, our research not only advances the frontier of gender identification methodologies in speech processing but also underscores the adaptability and efficacy of statistical modeling techniques in linguistically diverse contexts.

articleTitle: Detecting Infectious Disease Based on Social Media Data Using BERT Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Seasonal diseases are those diseases that are widespread during a particular time of the year including monsoons, winter etc. In the absence of preventative measures, the human race remains vulnerable to the hazardous effects of seasonal diseases following regular patterns of increased inci- dence and transmission which remains a global concern. Dengue, Influenza, etc. are such types of diseases where every year many people get affected globally. The primary focus of this research paper is to understand the opinion of people regarding the seasonal diseases. The research paper covers sentiment analysis on textual data from social media where people have vocalized their sentiments or thinking regarding seasonal diseases and seasonal infectious diseases. Influenza, Dengue, Malaria, Japanese Encephalitis, and Chikungunya are the seasonal diseases that have been covered in this research paper. To achieve this, the language model Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) was used to verify the sentiments about the seasonal diseases. The result of the investigation hold the potential to significantly enhance our comprehension of societal sentiments, discerning between states of tranquility and concern among individuals. The outcome of the study will help healthcare department to plan the necessary actions.

articleTitle: A Feature Selection Study on the Bot-IoT Dataset Using Ensemble Classification Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: IoT is an emerging giant in the field of technol- ogy, taking over traditional systems, providing interconnected- ness, convenience, efficiency, and automation, making our lives unimaginably better. However, security for these IoT systems is challenging, especially due to their interconnectedness, making them vulnerable to various cyber threats. The rising tide of IoT botnets, especially, presents a unique challenge. This has urgently increased the need for Intrusion Detection research. Modern Intrusion Detection approaches often employ Machine Learning for effective results. Feature Selection is extremely important while creating Machine Learning Classification models to avoid overfitting and poor performance. This paper focuses on running a Feature Selection study on the Bot-IoT dataset provided by UNSW to increase the accuracy of a ML model. The paper tests 5 types of Feature Selection methods, from Filter- based, Wrapper-based and Embedded methods, combined with two distinct ensemble classifiers: Random Forest + Adaboost and XGBoost. Each combination is tested with the dataset, and the accuracy is compared to find the most effective and versatile feature selection method that can assist both Stacking and Voting- type Ensemble classifiers. The results show that Karl Pearson can provide the best accuracy when applied to both Ensemble Classifiers.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Exploring Eye Gaze Patterns in Three Dimensions: An Innovative Visualization Dashboard
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Eye tracking is a method of measuring and analyzing the movements of the eyes as they move and focus on different objects in the visual field. This technique has been used in a wide range of fields, including psychology, neuroscience and human-computer interaction. Eye tracking provides valuable insights into how individuals process visual information, including attentional biases, cognitive processing, and decision-making. Traditionally, eye tracking has relied on licensed software and specialized hardware, making it costly and less accessible for some researchers and applications. However, with recent technological advancements and by leveraging the capabilities of webcams, researchers, and practitioners can now perform eye-tracking experiments without the need for expensive equipment. By utilizing webcams, researchers can conduct eye-tracking experiments in a cost-effective manner, making the method more accessible to a broader range of researchers and practitioners.

articleTitle: AI and Blockchain-Based Collaborative Architecture for Safeguarding IoT-Driven Water Treatment Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: This study introduces a novel method for monitoring water quality using combined Artificial Intelligence (AI) and blockchain technology. Our approach recognizes the vital importance of water for life and habitats, incorporating a variety of AI algorithms, such as Decision Tree, Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and perceptron. The use of these algorithms provides an invaluable opportunity for an in-depth study of water quality data and detection of deviant values, as well as forecasting and prevention of threats. This paper looks at these dynamics, presenting a new paradigm; we employed AI-infused techniques to unveil hidden patterns in data while using blockchain technology as a means for securing data transactions. For training the AI algorithms, we utilized a benchmark dataset of smart water treatment plants that comprised of malicious and non-malicious sensor data. The trained AI models can efficiently bifurcate malicious and non-malicious sensor data so that treatment plants can operate effectively. Further, the non-malicious data is forwarded to the blockchain network, where different water-related organizations are associated with water quality checking, improving human life expectancy. Lastly, the proposed architecture is evaluated using different evaluation metrics, such as training accuracy, log-loss curve, validation curve, and blockchain bandwidth graph.

articleTitle: Agricultural AI Alliance: Federated Learning CNNs for Papaya Leaf Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: However, precision agriculture has successfully used Federated Learning (FL) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), especially in plant pathology. This paper presents a novel FL-CNN model currently used to classify papaya leaf diseases into four levels. This model enhances early disease detection and facilitates specific agricultural interventions. We employed federated averaging, wherein the local information was consolidated into a single global model whereby client data was secured and confidentiality maintained as collective intelligence prevailed. The result analysis showed that macros, micros, and weighted average precision-recall scores were 0.98621357. The macro, micro, and weighted averages in the model for client vl_1 are 91.95% and 91. Client vl_2 demonstrated considerable improvement with 94.25% and 94.21 % mean scores. Client vl_3 showed further progress, averaging 96.42 %, 96.39%, and 70%. The learner identified by vl_ 4 demonstrated continuous improvement, having mean scores of 96.75%, 96.74, and 96.83%. It brings out the fact that the FL strategy is effective. This pattern was at its peak in client vl_5, which reached the highest mean values of 97.56%, 97.S38% and besides, they confirm that the FL-CNN model adapts to changes and learns slowly from gradually added data. Federated averaging has proven its capability to incorporate local data insights into a global data framework, improving scalability with agricultural district surveillance privacy awareness. The accuracy of the FL-CNN model for classifying papaya leaf disease from all severity levels is a vital factor significantly impacting the treatment of this disorder. It offers a new way of perceiving and combating the threat.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach for Predictive Maintenance Monitoring of Aircraft Engines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: The realm of aircraft maintenance involves predictive maintenance, which utilizes historical data and machine parts' performance to anticipate the need for maintenance activities. The primary focus of this paper is to delve into the application of predictive maintenance of aircraft gas turbine engines. Our methodology involves assigning a randomly chosen deterioration value and monitoring the change in flow and efficiency over time. By carefully analyzing these factors, we can deduce whether the engines are at fault and whether their condition will deteriorate further. The ultimate objective is to identify potential engine malfunctions early to prevent future accidents. Recent years have witnessed the emergence of multiple machine learning and deep learning algorithms to predict the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of engines. The precision and accuracy of these algorithms in assessing the performance of aircraft engines are pretty promising. We have incorporated a hybrid model on various time series cycles to enhance their efficacy further. Employing data collected from 21 sensors, we can predict the remaining useful life of the turbine engines with greater precision and accuracy.

articleTitle: waRLOCK: Countering Ransomware and Data Leak
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: In an era marked by the evolution of cybercrime from isolated hackers to highly organized enterprises, the surge in ransomware attacks presents a pressing concern. Enter RLOCK (pronounced as warlock), a meticulously crafted system that employs a novel reverse monitoring approach, actively transforming data to self-destruct, offering proactive protection against ransomware and data leaks. RLOCK revolutionizes the fight against ransomware by implementing continuous monitoring of specific files, prioritizing data resilience in hostile environments. Additionally, the challenge of protection against data leaks is met with a proactive solution. Imagine the peace of mind that comes with the knowledge that, even in the event of a data breach, the compromised information will self-destruct when accessed on an unauthorized system. Through RLOCK's data transformation, data can discern its environment, triggering self-destruction upon authentication failure. Discover a new paradigm in cybersecurity with RLOCK.

articleTitle: Enhancing Micro Electro Mechanical System Gyroscope Data Precision Through Autoencoder-Based Denoising
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Micro Electro Mechanical System gyroscopes, used predominantly in the aerospace industry, utilize a vibrating structure to measure the rate of rotation. The performance of these gyroscopes is affected by random drift noises. Various methods have been employed to denoise the gyroscope output. This paper proposes a robust Deep Learning model, leveraging auto encoders implemented in both Linear and Convolutional Neural Network architectures, to denoise the gyroscope data. In a post-processing analysis using the sensor's original data, the DL based denoising model shows a significant improvement in short term stability, demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing the overall robustness and accuracy of the gyroscope measurements. Metrics such as standard deviation and Peak Signal to Noise Ratio are employed to measure the effectiveness of the denoising models in enhancing the quality of gyroscope data. The robustness of the proposed architecture is also assessed in terms of its computational complexity and efficiency. The performance of the model is compared with conventional methods like the Kalman Filter, Principal Component Analysis, and Empirical Mode Decomposition. The results show that the autoencoder model exhibits superior denoising and better computational efficiency compared to the conventional approaches.

articleTitle: Enhancing Online Safety: Automated Hate Speech Detection on Instagram with BERT-powered Model and Real-time Moderation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative hate speech detection model tailored for Instagram, utilizing the powerful Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) model. Through a meticulous integration of BERT with an elaborate data collection strategy and refined methodology, the study seeks to enhance precision and recall, mitigating false positives and negatives, thereby fostering a safer and more inclusive online environment on Instagram. Addressing the existing research gap, the model distinguishes itself by incorporating real-world context and addressing nuanced language nuances often missed by current hate speech detection models. The HateXplain dataset is employed for training and validation, complemented by a web scraping strategy for collecting real-time Instagram comments via the “Insc” extension. The BERT model undergoes fine-tuning to adapt to Instagram-specific language patterns.
