The comprehensive methodology spans data selection, training, and integration with Instagram, classification, evaluation, and real-time deployment. The anticipated contributions and findings include the model's superiority in accuracy and performance metrics, such as precision, recall, and F1-score, and its effectiveness in detecting diverse forms of hate speech while maintaining robustness. Comparative analysis showcases the advantages of BERT over LSTM models in terms of accuracy and contextual understanding. The paper suggests future directions, urging exploration of multilingual support, user profile integration for enhanced context, and experimentation with multi-modal hate speech detection incorporating images and videos. In summary, this paper offers a promising avenue for combating hate speech on Instagram, striving to contribute to the creation of a safer and more inclusive online community.

articleTitle: Cognitive Farming in Agriculture: Deploying CNN-RF for Maize Disease Precision Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: A hybrid approach integrating both CNN and RF is investigated in this research study of the Survey regarding the classification of maize leaf diseases with the help of CNN and RF. Our research carefully contrasts five created disease severities as a reported diagnostic tool for agriculturalists. The high accuracy of the model was extensively validated by applying various performance metrics with excellent precision of the different classes ranging from 95.90% to 98.47% for recall ranged between 95.01% to 99.21%, and F1- scores ranged between 96.55% to 98.4. The model achieved a general accuracy of 97.42851 %. We employed various averaging approaches to generalize the performance results across varying illness levels. A macro average yielded an accuracy of 97.37%, recall of 97.48%, and F1-score of 97.42%, implying similarity of performance across classes. Considering class imbalance, the weighted average was accurate at 97.44%, recalled at 97.43%, and the F1-score was similar at 97.43%. The micro average, as the aggregation of results across classes, was remarkably stable at 97.43 %, representing the performance of the model well and especially favoring frequent courses. Early identification and classification of diseases affecting maize leaves significantly contributed to precision agriculture, and this paper presents a reliable and efficient method for a timely diagnosis. It shows the stable performance of the CNN-RF model because many statistical measures are indicated. This implies that it possesses reasonable practicality in agricultural applications that highly support pest control and increase crop yields.

articleTitle: Epilepsy Detection Using Supervised Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: In the current scenario, people are suffering and isolated by themselves by seizure detection and prediction in epilepsy. Also, it is highly essential that it needs to be identified through wearable devices. Researchers discussed this issue and outlined future developments in this field, suggesting that Machine Learning (ML) techniques could radically change how we diagnose and manage patients with epilepsy. However, as data availability has increased, Deep Learning (DL) techniques have become the most cutting-edge approach to adopt and use with wearable devices. On the other hand, large amounts of data are needed to train DL models, making overfitting problematic. DL models are created with open-source toolboxes and Python, allowing researchers to create automated systems and broaden computational accessibility. This work thoroughly overviews deep learning (DL) methods and neuroimaging modalities for automated epileptic seizure identification. It covers several MRI and EEG techniques for epileptic seizure diagnosis and treatment programmes designed to treat these seizures. The study also covers the difficulties in precise detection, the benefits and drawbacks of DL-based strategies, potential DL models and upcoming research in this area.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithms for Profitable Stock Trading Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) techniques are gaining strong interest in developing stock trading strategies, given their ability to learn profitable behaviors in complex environments. This paper presents a comparative study evaluating deep RL algorithms, including DQN, Double DQN (DDQN), Dueling Double DQN (Dueling DDQN), and Rainbow DQN, on financial stock trading problems based on historical price data. The performance of each algorithm is analyzed using metrics such as cumulative rewards earned, value function stability measured through Q-values, and loss over the training period, indicating sample efficiency. We benchmark extensions like Rainbow DQN that integrate multiple optimization mechanisms against conventional DQN methods. We discuss the capabilities of these state-of-the-art techniques along with current limitations and challenges that need to be addressed through further research. The results on out-of-sample datasets over validation periods provide guidelines for real-world applicability. The insights from this empirical analysis can inform the design of improved stock trading agents using deep reinforcement learning.

articleTitle: Watershed Segmentation with Gradient Vista and SOBEL-Crafted Contours for Analyzing EMDS-6 Microbial Environmental Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: The aim of this research is to present a comprehensive framework for image analysis applied to the EMDS-6 dataset to help identify microorganisms in environmental studies. In order to identify and quantify diverse environmental microorganisms, a reliable methodology is required. Even under the heterogeneous imaging conditions inherent in the EMDS-6 dataset, the proposed methodology proved effective in delineating microorganism boundaries and isolating clustered entities. A framework for image analysis of the EMDS-6 dataset was developed to reliably recognize and quantify a variety of environmental microorganisms. Pre-processing of the images, precision edge detection with SOBEL contours, and advanced segmentation of Graduate Vista Watersheds are among the methods used. Using this combination of techniques, microorganism boundaries can be precisely defined and clustered entities can be isolated across heterogeneous EMDS-6 imaging conditions. According to our methodology, the pipeline classified microorganisms with 93% accuracy, focused edges with 55% Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio, and segmented objects with 95% Jaccard Index. Compared to baseline approaches, qualitative results indicate considerable improvements in signal localization, feature representation, and region identification. To automate the recognition of species and parsing of complex microbiology images, customized computer vision and stability-driven propagation methods hold great promise. Smart imaging systems will soon be capable of screening environmental samples rapidly, identifying salient organisms, and adapting to detect emerging agents based on this knowledge.

articleTitle: Modeling of Challenges to Industry 4.0 in E-waste Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: In terms of managing e-waste, Industry 4.0 (I4.0) offers several advantages, including tracking and tracing products and monitoring sustainable practices. However, industries continue to face several implementation-related difficulties. Twenty-five articles were reviewed to find challenges. A group of five experts was assembled to confirm the challenges that had been noted. As a result, the seven most critical challenges are identified. These seven challenges are lack of infrastructure, lack of technical skills, high initial capital, resistance to change, top management, fear of losing sensitive information, and lack of collaboration among stakeholders. The cause-effect group of identified challenges was categorized and given a priority ranking using the Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation (DEMATEL) methodology. According to the results, top management commitment and a lack of infrastructure are the most pressing issues. Industries should concentrate on cause-related challenges because they have an impact on effect-related challenges. The novelty of the current study is that it could be the first study that is focused on I4.0 in e-waste management context. Therefore, the proposed study could be helpful for practitioners for the adoption of I4.0 in e-waste management context.

articleTitle: Quantum Exploration in Ransomware Detection with Conventional Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Ransomware attacks are a significant and evolving cybersecurity threat that requires innovative and efficient detection methods. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of the performance of quantum machine learning (QML) models versus traditional machine learning techniques. In particular, the focus is on the evaluation of three QML models (VQC, Pegasos QSVM, and Quantum-augmented SVM) that have not yet been studied in the context of ransomware detection. This study examines in detail the effectiveness and resource utilization of traditional machine learning models (SVM, decision trees, XGBoost) using a dynamic ransomware database. To assess the efficacy of our model, we compare performance metrics like F1 score, recall, accuracy, and precision. The study also illustrates how training and testing times for quantum and classical models differ. The study addresses current problems and highlights the potential and limitations of OML.

articleTitle: Unveiling the Art of Effective Learning through Spaced Repetition and Evidence-Based Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: This study critically examines the limitations of traditional learning methods, such as cramming, re-reading, and massed practice, which often result in suboptimal long-term retention and understanding. The paper proposes an integrated approach, emphasizing the pivotal role of Spaced Repetition alongside other evidence-based techniques. By exploring Active Recall, Desirable Difficulties, Elaboration, Interleaving, Concrete Examples, Dual Coding, and Distributed Practice, this research harmonizes cognitive psychology and neuroscience principles. The integrated approach outlined in the paper aims to enhance memory, comprehension, and problem-solving, catering to learners of diverse paces and abilities. The essence of evidence-based learning is embodied in the strategies presented, promising effective and enduring knowledge acquisition. Ultimately, this paper offers insights for educators and students, demonstrating practical applications for teaching and learning that leverage these evidence-based techniques, particularly emphasizing the significance of Spaced Repetition.

articleTitle: Advancing Farming Practices: Machine Learning Algorithms for Optimal Crop Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: This study underscores the critical importance of the agricultural sector for ensuring global food security and economic resilience, emphasizing the role of machine learning (ML)-enhanced crop recommendation systems. These systems are increasingly crucial for guiding farmers in choosing crops that are best suited to their unique soil and environmental conditions. Through the analysis of a comprehensive dataset, including soil composition, climate variations, historical crop yields, and agricultural practices, this research evaluates the performance of several ML algorithms–such as neural networks, decision trees, random forests, and support vector machines–in forecasting the most appropriate crops. Training on historical data allows these algorithms to decipher the complex dynamics between environmental factors and crop results. The success of these models is gauged by metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. This study also delves into the models' interpretability, offering crucial insights to both agricultural practitioners and researchers. Moreover, it presents the creation of a user-friendly web application that applies these ML models to provide personalized crop recommendations, requiring user inputs like geographical location, soil characteristics, and weather data. The findings reveal that ML algorithms can significantly empower farmers with knowledge to select suitable crops, thereby boosting agricultural efficiency, optimizing the use of resources, and enhancing the sustainability of agricultural operations. The research highlights the necessity of selecting the right ML algorithms and preprocessing techniques for achieving superior results. Notably, we have enhanced the accuracy of the random forest algorithm to 99.92% and ADABOOST with the Decision Tree Classifier to 99.02%. This contribution to precision agriculture showcases the practical use of ML in crop recommendation systems as a technological approach to addressing agricultural sector challenges and bolstering the global food supply chain.

articleTitle: Integrated Automated Attendance System with RFID, Wi-Fi, and Visual Recognition Technology for Enhanced Classroom Security and Precise Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: The integrated automated smart attendance system utilizes RFID, Wi-Fi, and visual recognition technologies to elevate classroom security and ensure precise monitoring of attendance records. It consolidates cutting-edge components such as RFID tags, ESP8266 Wi-Fi modules, ESP-32 CAM modules, solenoid locks, servo motors, and PIR sensors to devise a strong remedy. RFID technology enables accurate attendance tracking by assigning tags to students and faculty members. The Wi-Fi and visual recognition components enhance the system's functionalities, facilitating wireless connectivity, instantaneous data transfer, and validation of identities. Solenoid locks and servo motors ensure controlled access, responding to validated attendance records. PIR sensors detect motion, contrasting between genuine presence and proximity. The paper's methodology delineates the necessary hardware and software requirements, procedures for system initialization, testing phases, establishment of server connectivity, implementation of access control mechanisms, and formulation of end-of-session protocols. It highlights the successful integration and validation of hardware components, backend connectivity, identity confirmation, attendance recording, data encryption, and session termination procedures. The research aims to modernize attendance tracking in educational settings, improving efficiency, accuracy, and security while appreciating the need for further adaptation to suit diverse educational environments for broader adoption and sustained advancement.

articleTitle: Novel Methodology of Adaptive Machine Learning and Deep Learning System for Detecting the Fraudulent Activities in Financial Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: In the development of mobile Internet technology, both mobile payment fraud and data transaction fraud have dramatically increased in recent years. Financial fraud is a severe global issue that has severely harmed financial market growth. However, it can be difficult to identify fraud with highly imbalanced datasets. Furthermore, fraud transaction causes high financial suffering for financial institutions and consumers. Therefore, an effectual fraud recognition model is needed to detect financial fraud in the financial field. As a result, this paper aims to establish a model for identifying financial fraud using techniques such as deep learning and machine learning. To begin with, the financial information is sourced from online data repositories. in addition, the important attributes/traits/features discerned from the provided details are This text was obtained by utilizing the Principal Component Analysis (PCA) technique. A method or approach. Afterwards, the obtained characteristics go through a process of being examined or investigated. This text is given as input to both the deep learning model and the machine learning model. other deep-learning frameworks can adaptively learn and process complex patterns, such as images and text. These systems have the ability to adjust and improve their performance over time through training and feedback. In the field of deep learning, there is a type of neural network called Adaptive Residual Long Short-Term Memory (A-ResLSTM) used to identify fraudulent behavior. In order to improve the identification. In order to improve efficiency, the MLP and ResLSTM parameters are adjusted. Through the utilization of the Reptile Search Algorithm (RSA). Finally, the proposed model is validated through various measures and compared with the classical detection models. Thus, the proposed model outperforms effective results for financial fraud detection.

articleTitle: Breast Cancer Image Classification: Leveraging Deep Learning and Large Language Models for Semantic Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Breast cancer, a significant global health problem that is mainly affecting women, demonstrates the importance of early detection to enhance survival rates. Medical image classification is a significant field that utilizes deep learning methods such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Region-Based CNNs (R-CNNs), and Deep Neural Networks (DNNs). Despite this, challenges such as over fitting persist, particularly with limited data or complex models. Although these models learn hierarchical features, interpreting them in intricate image structures is still challenging and complicates decision rationale. To address this, we propose a comprehensive approach for breast cancer image classification. The initial process involves image segmentation using CNN to identify regions of interest, followed by precise object detection with OpenCV. Data quality and diversity are ensured by preprocessing and augmentation with ImageDataGenerator, while informative features are extracted using the InceptionV3model. Our analysis of textual descriptions and embeddings is done by integrating Sentence Transformers and CLIP from the Large Language Model (LLM) framework. Achieving robust decision-making is ensured by setting a threshold of 0.7 for image classification based on predicted malignancy probability. Finally, improving the computations of similarity scores can improve prediction accuracy for reliable diagnostic interpretations. An accuracy of 0.92 in breast cancer diagnosis is guaranteed by integrating LLM and CNN for classification.

articleTitle: Enhanced Multi-Class Fetal Plane Detection with Limb Localization in Ultrasound Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: In this novel study, we address the critical need for automated interpretation and analysis of ultrasound images in the context of fetal development assessment. The current large-scale retrospective analyses suffer from the laborious and specialized process of manually identifying standard fetal ultrasound planes, requiring sonographer expertise. Our innovative approach leverages state-of-the-art deep-learning techniques, specifically vision transformers, to automate the detection of standard fetal ultrasound planes. Our methodology involves the integration of two datasets, with a particular emphasis on musculoskeletal planes, notably fetal limbs. The resulting comprehensive classification model comprises eight distinct classes: fetal limbs, fetal abdomen, fetal thorax, fetal femur, maternal cervix, and fetal arms. Notably, the application of vision transformers, specifically ViT -L16 (Vision Transformer), to mid-pregnancy prenatal screening achieved a remarkable test accuracy of 97.2%. The primary goal of incorporating vision transformers into prenatal screening is to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of identifying critical anatomical structures. This advancement facilitates the prompt evaluation of fetal growth metrics and enables early identification of irregularities. Serving as a valuable tool for ultrasound technicians, our study signifies a significant leap in transforming the assessment of fetal well-being through ultrasound techniques. Moreover, it sets new benchmarks for detecting abnormal fetal development within ultrasound visuals, contributing to the ongoing evolution of fetal health assessment methodologies.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Intra-Cluster Routing Protocol Optimized for Object Recognition and Tracing Framework Within WSNs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: One of the major purposes of wireless sensor networks (WSNs) is recognizing things and monitoring. The main problems with the algorithm are the reliability of the adaptation, recognizing objects, and network longevity. In order to guarantee the superior caliber of the support, a balance should be struck among energy, economy and detection precision, which are difficult in a WSN with limited resources. The majority of studies have increased the lifetime of the tool at the expense of high density of nodes in order to achieve target recognition precision. Neither the object localization precision nor the overall cost were taken into account. By restricting the detection to a predetermined target direction, some researchers were able to achieve low energy consumption while maintaining object identification precision. Specifically, several studies restricted their attention to node sequencing and node grouping for conservation of energy. Our study suggests the Energy Efficient Object Detection and Tracking Framework (EEODTF) for homogeneous WSNs, a mobile architecture for identifying and tracking objects that reduces the usage of energy during monitoring without compromising the precision of object recognition and identification. Node optimization, mobile node trajectory optimization, node clustering, data reporting improvement, and identification improvement are the main strategies used to achieve energy-efficiency objectives.

Author Keywords: the Energy Efficient Object Detection and Tracking Framework

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing of Hybrid Power System Using Genetic Algorithm Based Partial Reinforcement Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Reducing dependency on traditional energy sources and meeting energy demands in an environmentally sustainable manner are two benefits of using renewable energy sources (RES). But RESs' unpredictability presents a big obstacle and reduces the system's dependability. Thus, reliability is the main issue with the hybrid RESs system, and it has to be resolved at the lowest possible cost to the customers. Heuristic optimization models have been widely used by academics to optimize hybrid RESs because of the shortcomings of formal methodologies. When compared to formal procedures, the main benefit of adopting meta-heuristic techniques is their capacity to handle difficult optimization problems in normal or minimal computational time. Hence in this work, genetic algorithm (GA) based partial reinforcement optimizer (PRO) is proposed for optimum sizing of hybrid power system.

articleTitle: Towards a Model: Examining the Positive Associations of Warmth, Competence, and Familiarity with Musicians' Attitudes Towards AI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: This study investigates attitudes towards AI musicians through a Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) approach. Data analysis focuses on the interplay between Anthropomorphism Degree (AD), Listening Type (LT), Warmth (W), Competence (C), Attitude (A), and Familiarity (F). The sample comprises 211 valid responses from college students, exploring perceptions via a questionnaire. Results indicate significant positive associations between attitudes towards AI and Competence, Familiarity, and Warmth. However, predictive validity analysis suggests caution in relying solely on the PLS-SEM model. Importance-Performance Analysis (IPMA) highlights competence as the primary influencer of attitudes towards AI, emphasizing its critical role over Warmth and Familiarity. This study contributes to understanding the nuanced dimensions of human interactions with AI musicians.

articleTitle: Priority-driven Unbalanced Transportation Problem (PUTP) to obtain better Initial Feasible Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: In this paper, we tackle the Priority-driven Unbalanced Transportation Problem (PUTP), a scenario where total demand exceeds total supply. An innovative algorithm, the Penalty-driven Priority-driven Unbalanced Transportation Problem (PPUTP) is introduced to solve this challenge. PPUTP allocates supplies to high-priority demands by computing penalties and sequentially addressing the most penalized demands, thereby ensuring priority demands are met efficiently. A comparative analysis with Vogel's Approximation Method (VAM) across various problem sets ranging from 5x5 to 50x50 dimensions demonstrates the efficiency of our algorithms. PPUTP consistently shows lower percentage increments from the optimal solution, indicating its robustness in providing near-optimal solutions. This study highlights the importance of algorithm selection based on problem set dimensions and complexity in Priority-driven Unbalanced Transportation Problem, with PPUTP emerging as a versatile and robust solution across various scenarios.

articleTitle: Robotic Process Automation: In-Depth Analysis of Advanced Automation Techniques and Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Robotic Process Automation (RPA) is a revolutionary technology that has swiftly transformed the landscape of modern business operations. RPA leverages software robots to automate repetitive, rule-based tasks, offering organizations the potential to enhance efficiency, reduce operational costs, and liberate human workers from mundane chores. This comprehensive research paper delves into the multifaceted realm of RPA, providing an extensive examination of its definition, applications across diverse industries, and its multitude of benefits and challenges. The paper also scrutinizes the prospects of RPA, emphasizing the integration of cognitive and artificial intelligence, the concept of hyper-automation, and its role in Industry 4.0 and the Internet of Things. Moreover, it addresses the ethical considerations surrounding RPA adoption, focusing on job displacement, data privacy, bias, transparency, and accountability. As businesses navigate the path to automation, this paper offers invaluable insights into RPA's transformative potential and its implications for the future of work and industry.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network Based Yield Phenotyping Framework: Fruit Grading and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: This research paper instigates an Artificial Intelligence-based Yield Phenotyping Framework tuned for fruit classification and grading. Fruit species exhibit homogeneity in color, shape, and size qualities, resulting in fruit grading and segmentation tasks on such datasets being counterproductive and vulnerable. The primary objective of this research paper is to establish a real-time, non-destructive system that automates fruit segmentation, grading and classification. Here, we use two different datasets and conduct a detailed analysis of the architectures of two deep learning models: AlexNet and ResNet. Different kinds of fruits are added to the proposed prototype. Videos of each fruit is recorded and sent to a local server. Deep learning models predict the fruit grade, and the system's conveyor belt sort the fruits into baskets based on their grade. By using preprocessing techniques, we can precisely isolate the fruit in each image. This study considers evaluation metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall and f1-score to evaluate the deep learning algorithm models. The ResNet architecture enables research to achieve a peak accuracy, precision and recall of 99%. This paper presents research surrounding the proposed prototype's architecture, methodologies, and experimental results and therefore provides an automated solution to an existing challenge in the Agri-field management.

articleTitle: Road Network Identification in Satellite Imagery using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: In the pursuit of enhancing road network detection from satellite imagery, this paper implements semantic segmentation techniques on the DeepGlobe Road Extraction dataset. Our approach entailed preprocessing the data with one-hot encoding for masks, followed by a training and validation split, and augmenting the training set to improve model robustness. Two prominent image segmentation architectures, namely DeepLabV3+ and U-Net, are compared and analyzed. DeepLabV3+ with a ResNet50 encoder is utilized for its advanced encoder-decoder structure, adept at capturing significant features and delineating road boundaries. A U-Net model is constructed, emphasizing a symmetrical encoderdecoder design. Both models underwent training with suitable parameters, loss functions, and learning rate schedules. Model performance is evaluated on the validation set, leveraging metrics such as the Intersection over Union score and Dice loss. The results, including normal accuracy metrics and binary cross entropy loss, are visualized to compare the original satellite imagery, ground truth masks, and predicted segmentation. Performance analysis of both the deep learning models show promising results, thus highlighting the effectiveness of the applied methodologies in road network detection and segmentation.

articleTitle: Optimizing Digital Marketing Strategies Through Search Engine Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: This article examines SEO and its significance in digital marketing. The goal is to comprehend the main elements that impact achieving high rankings in search engines and the consequences of the presence of websites. Additionally, it strives to study its influence on website visibility, organic traffic, and rank in search results. This document comprehensively examines search engine optimization techniques, including optimizing website content and external factors, optimizing textual materials, and enhancing technical factors. Moreover, it examines the connection between SEO and UX (user experience). It emphasizes the significance of maximizing user happiness and participation. The document further explores the possible future of search engine optimization and online advertising. It contains new trends, expected challenges, and advice for future investigations and real-world applications. In general, the main objective of this paper is to present valuable viewpoints regarding the realm of SEO and its importance in the digital promotion arena.

articleTitle: Predicting Song Popularity Using Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: In today's music landscape, predicting a song's success is crucial for musicians, record labels, and streaming platforms. This paper introduces a methodology for estimating popularity using Spotify data, termed the “Proxy Popularity Score.” Three models – Random Forest, LightGBM Regressor, and XGBoost Regressor – are utilized for prediction. Performance metrics including mean absolute error, mean squared error, root mean squared error, and R-squared error are employed to evaluate model accuracy. Correlation values of 99.85%, 99.87%, and 99.84% are achieved for XGBoost, LightGBM, and Random Forest respectively. The study concludes with a ranking of songs based on predicted popularity scores.

articleTitle: Location-Based Ideal Site Selection using Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Selecting a business site is a significant decision in managing a commercial organization. It becomes more complex in countries like India, where population density is high, and it is tough to distribute services fairly. With this difficulty, investing in a location without a thorough survey is challenging. This study aims to provide an information map that can help choose the optimal neighborhood for a particular business. The research aims to use data science powers to provide an unsupervised machine-learning approach to offer a recommendation-based solution that suggests the best location for a given use case. The objective of this paper is the in-depth analysis for site-finding that includes clustering regions based on various factors such as geographical locations (like schools, bus and railway stations, and hospitals), sanitation, distance, footfall, and other entities. The idea is to obtain the user's use case query and then create hotspots on the map that show the most suitable locations where the specific use case will benefit the stakeholders the most. We need to identify neighborhoods where there may be an unsatisfied need for Indian restaurants. Additionally, we require places that are uncrowded and have little competition. If the first two requirements are satisfied, we would also like a location close to a prominent city neighborhood. The advantages of each area will then be clearly expressed so that stakeholders can choose the best possible final location.

articleTitle: Blockchain Based Security System for Health Care
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Security in healthcare systems based on blockchain technology is the subject of ongoing research. Block Chain technology has the potential to revolutionize many different sectors since it provides a decentralized, incontestable, and publicly verifiable record of every transaction activity. Bitcoin's foundational mechanism is referred to as “block chain technology.” This technology allows for completely decentralized transaction processing. Healthcare aims to diagnose, treat, relieve, and cure any and all bodily and mental health issues, as well as to promote health and prevent sickness. Since all transactions in a blockchain are encrypted, it provides the highest level of security possible. Blockchain networks provide the same assurance of security for medical records. The integrity of the network's ledgers may be checked by checking file signatures on each node to make sure no alterations have been performed. The signature will no longer be valid when the record has been modified. The future of blockchain and big data applications is promising. Big Data technology can manage any kind, amount, or speed of data, while blockchain enhances efficiency across all industries. It has been noticed that medical records are maintained on a blockchain for reasons of security. Proposed system has evaluated healthcare data for security. When compared to the results of cutting-edge research, however, the scalability and adaptability of traditional methods are clearly lacking. Better performance and security utilizing blockchain technology is essential, hence developing such a system is a priority.

articleTitle: Detection of DoS Attacks Using Machine Learning Based Intrusion Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Conventional intrusion detection systems are not always sufficient due to the increasing sophistication and frequency of Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks. This work presents a novel solution to this problem by leveraging machine learning techniques to increase the precision and efficacy of real-time intrusion detection. The system keeps a careful eye on network traffic patterns, looking for any irregularities that would point to a denial-of-service attack. An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) that utilizes machine learning technologies—specifically, neural networks and support vector machines—allows for real-time adaptation to new attack patterns. A combination of rigorous simulations and real-world testing provides empirical support for the IDS's quick detection and mitigation of DoS threats. This initiative makes a major contribution to the development of cybersecurity defenses.

articleTitle: Detecting and Locating Image Forgeries with Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: It is becoming more important to have reliable methods for identifying picture forgeries, particularly passive forging techniques like copy-move and splicing, since the proliferation of digital images across a variety of platforms has raised the urgency of the situation. The purpose of this research is to explicitly target passive forgery tactics by presenting a unique strategy that makes use of deep learning approaches for the purpose of accurately identifying modified areas inside photographs. The methodology that we have suggested makes use of Mobile Net and ResNet as feature extraction networks. It does this by extracting rich representations from picture data in order to identify complicated patterns that are suggestive of possible manipulations, such as copy-move and splicing manipulations. We make use of Mask R-CNN, which is a cutting-edge instance segmentation model, in order to precisely localize and quantify forged areas. This allows us to calculate the proportion of changed material that is included inside photos.

articleTitle: Predicting Stock Market Movements with Linear Regression and LSTM Machine Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: The prediction of stock prices remains a perpetual challenge and opportunity in the domain of finance and investment. In this study, we delve into the realm of machine learning, employing both Linear Regression and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models, to tackle the intricate task of stock price forecasting. Our research centers on two datasets: Google (GOOGL) and Tesla (TSLA), sourced from Kaggle, with the aim of providing a comprehensive evaluation of model performance and gaining insights into their practical utility. Our findings reveal variations in model performance across the datasets. LSTM models excel in capturing intricate temporal patterns, yielding remarkably low MSE and MAE values. With R-squared values close to unity, LSTM models exhibit a strong ability to explain variance in stock prices. These results underscore the potential of deep learning, particularly LSTM, to enhance stock price prediction accuracy. The implications extend to investment strategies and technical analysis. This research contributes to the ongoing discussion on stock price prediction, offering insights into the efficacy of machine learning models and their relevance in financial decision-making.

articleTitle: Potato Plant Leaf Diseases Classification using Neural Network Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Throughout the process of plant development, there is a possibility of encountering diseases that can negatively affect the production of crops. Additionally, farmers may experience challenges in terms of overall yield and income rates. However, numerous advantages can be obtained by early identification and classification of these diseases. The advancements in contemporary technology have proven advantageous in categorizing plant diseases. This report aims to introduce a system for classifying plant diseases, specifically emphasizing potato plant leaves. The classification system utilizes neural network-based techniques, specifically the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models. The model classifies potato leaves into three categories, namely healthy leaves, early blight, and late blight. This system utilizes two CNN models- AlexNet and GoogLeN et, to carry out the classification process. To assess AlexNet's and GoogLeNet's performance, images of potato leaves are obtained from the Kaggle dataset. The results of the experiment demonstrate that the classification accuracy of potato plant leaf diseases by the system is 96.4 % for the AlexNet model and 97.0% accuracy for the GoogLeNet model.

articleTitle: Machine Learning's Transformative Role in Human Activity Recognition Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Human action recognition (HAR) is a burgeoning field of computer vision that seeks to automatically understand and classify the intricate movements performed by humans. From the graceful leaps of a ballerina to the decisive strides of a surgeon, HAR aims to decipher the language of motion, unlocking a plethora of potential applications. This abstract delves into the core of HAR, highlighting its key challenges and promising avenues for advancement. We begin by outlining the various modalities used for action recognition, such as RGB videos, depth sensors, and skeletal data, each offering unique perspectives on the human form. Next, we delve into the diverse set of algorithms employed for HAR, ranging from traditional machine learning techniques to the burgeoning realm of deep learning. We explore the strengths and limitations of each approach, emphasizing the crucial role of feature extraction and model selection in achieving accurate recognition. Challenges in Human Action Recognition (HAR), such as intra-class variations, inter-class similarities, and environmental factors. Ongoing efforts include robust feature development and contextual integration. The paper envisions HAR's future impact on healthcare, robotics, video surveillance, and augmented reality, presenting an invitation to explore the transformative world of human action recognition and its potential to enhance our interaction with technology.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning and DL Approach to Marathi Sentiment Analysis Using Senticnet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: In the era of digital communication, understanding public sentiment is crucial. However, sentiment analysis tools for less common languages like Marathi are limited. This paper introduces a machine learning and deep learning approach to Marathi sentiment analysis using Senticnet. Through the utilization of Senticnet and various machine learning techniques, we collected and pre-processed data, adapt Senticnet for Marathi, and design language-specific sentiment analysis models. Leveraging techniques such as tokenization, text cleaning, and feature extraction, we effectively classified Marathi text into positive, negative, and neutral sentiments. Our library's performance is evaluated against existing tools, show casing its accuracy and sensitivity to Marathi sentiment nuances. This work not only enhances Marathi sentiment analysis but also offers insights into adapting resources for non-english languages. By sharing our methodology and library, we encourage further research in regional languages, promoting sentiment analysis in diverse linguistic landscapes. The significant this research focuses on the creation of robust Marathi sentiment analysis tool, facilitating deeper understanding and analysis of sentiments in underrepresented languages, and serving as a catalyst for future advancements in sentiment analysis across linguistic boundaries.

articleTitle: Flask Powered Heart Health Predictor Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Heart Health Predictor Using Flask is an innovative web application that integrates Flask as its front end and Python as its back end. Ideal for healthcare professionals and individuals, it forecasts heart disease risk through a seamless fusion of Flask for data input and Python for machine learning. With cardiovascular disease claiming a life every minute, automating prediction becomes crucial. In medical care, information science manages vast data, addressing the complexity of coronary disease prediction. Utilizing a cardiac disease dataset from the UCI AI repository. The research presented here employs AI algorithms—Light GBM, AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting, XG Boost, and Random Forests—to predict and categorize the likelihood of coronary sickness. The study, providing a relative report on algorithm performance, reveals Light GBM's exceptional accuracy of 90%, making it a promising solution for enhancing predictive capabilities in heart health.

articleTitle: A Novel Human Activity Recognition Using Spiking Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: This research is primarily focused on Human Activity Recognition (HAR). HAR aims to forecast a user's daily activities by analyzing time series data collected from wearable sensors. However, contemporary behavioral datasets often overlook an essential aspect of phone listening activity, which is a central focus of this research. Additionally, most existing research in behavioral classification has not considered energy optimization through Artificial Neural Network (ANN) models. To address these gaps, this study introduces a dataset capturing human responses to phone calls and proposes a behavior classification model employing Spiking Neural Networks (SNN s) to address these issues. The proposed solution is multifaceted, encompassing measures such as model accuracy, parameter count, and energy consumption. Our proposed model achieved outstanding performance, boasting an accuracy of 96.72% on our dataset and remarkable energy consumption of approximately 7.42×10-08 J/inf. Moreover, experimental results on two renowned datasets, SHAR and VCI HAR, affirm the method's efficacy, demonstrating its applicability beyond our specific dataset.

articleTitle: Malware Classification using LSTM-CF Framework for Disk Forensic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: In the current era, digital forensic investigators need specialized tools to extract digital footprints from hard disks. The number of crimes is rising dramatically. This has resulted in an increased number of unresolved cybercrime cases including malicious software, hacking and cyberfraud. Disk forensics or disk investigation is a massive task. It takes weeks to collect the traces of the 1TB hard drive and analyze them. It is a challenging task to detect reliable evidence because of the worldwide use and advancement of digital communication technologies. By using automated tools, only predictable areas of the disk are often investigated, and as a result, latent evidence in the hidden area might be missed. In this paper, we present Chaithu's Framework (CF) that gives us a clear picture of the steps to follow and implement a machine learning algorithm which is able to predict whether the request is related to malware or not by analyzing the large world Microsoft Malware Prediction dataset collected from Kaggle. It consists of a total of 7.8 million data samples with 84 features collected in real time from Windows 7,8,9 and 10 systems. Using predictive machine learning algorithms, frauds can be detected automatically and autonomous actions can be taken to prevent them.

articleTitle: Fast UAV- Image-based Person Re-Identification at the Edge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Person re-identification (re-id) has been widely used in various applications, such as security surveillance, the retail sector, and the military. Although companies that manufacture security surveillance equipment, such as Hikvision, Huawei, and NEC, have developed and deployed person re-ied systems in real life, this research topic still has several opening challenges, such as high memory usage and computation cost, processes at the edge and re-identification on aerial images. This problem is crucial for UAV-based person re-id applications in the military and security surveillance. This study proposes a deep person re-id model that can balance the tradeoff between accuracy and inference cost when implemented on the edge device and images captured from UAV. Although the mAP score of our proposed model is 2.48 % lower than that of the SOTA model, experimental results verify that our model-based inference cost is much better than the SOTA-model-based result. Indeed, our approach's RAM usage and processing time are 157 % and 528 % better than those of the Sota model, respectively. This result also points out that our proposed model meets the real-time requirement on the Jetson-Xavier-based edge device.

articleTitle: ACAC: Automatic Cardiac Arrhythmia Classification Based on 1D-Deep Resnet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Arrhythmias are infrequent irregularities in a person's heartbeat rhythm. They result from any disruption in the ordered pattern of the heart's expanding wave of excitation, a process heavily reliant on electrical activity. These arrhythmias might result in consequences that could be fatal and constitute a direct risk to life. As a result, detecting and classifying arrhythmias is a significant challenge in cardiac diagnostics. Electrocardiograms (ECG) are widely used in the diagnosis of arrhythmias because they are a low-cost, non-invasive, and rapid technique of diagnosis. However, the unpredictability of arrhythmic segments, along with the sensitivity of ECGs to noise, leads to arrhythmia misdiagnosis. Furthermore, manually identifying cardiac arrhythmias using ECG data takes time and is liable for inaccuracy. Deep learning (DL) is a preferred approach for fast and automatic ECG signal classification, surpassing the performance of traditional machine learning models. The suggested study proposes a novel deep learning architecture, namely t-dimensional deep residual neural network (1D-deep ResNet) for an Automatic cardiac arrhythmia classification (ACAC) system. ECG signals from the MIT -BIH dataset were used to train and evaluate the model. This proposed model contributes in two different ways. First, the unbalanced ECG data are corrected using the upsampling approach to reduce noise and prevent biased prediction outcomes. Next, the unbalanced ECG signals are automatically classified using 1D-Deep ResNet. ACAC system aims to overcome the issues of traditional electrocardiograms (ECGs) in the identification of arrhythmias, which can be impacted by noise and unpredictability of events, leading to misinterpretation and mistakes. The confusion matrix is used to calculate the model accuracy, AUC, precision, recall, and f1 score to evaluate the model performance. The results of the experiments shows that the proposed method performed well, with 99.9% and 99.94% AUC score in the training and testing datasets, respectively. The proposed model outperforms other existing deep learning approaches like CNN, LSTM, and GRU in terms of performance, and it will significantly minimise the involvement of doctors in the classification of ECG signals. According to our research findings, the 1D-deep ResNet is more suitable for automated cardiac arrhythmia classification in the future than other deep learning algorithms now available.

articleTitle: Precision Nutrition through Smart Wearable Technology Tailored Solutions for Personalized Health Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: The increasing prevalence of obesity and sedentary lifestyles has become a pressing global health issue, prompting the need for effective interventions to promote healthier habits. In response, there has been a growing emphasis on utilizing technology-driven approaches, as demonstrated by the introduction of the NutriWear system. This innovative system aims to provide personalized recommendations for dietary plans by analysing data from smartwatches and pathological insights. Through the integration of wearable devices, web application, and data storage, NutriWear offers tailored guidance and insights to improve overall health and well-being. Employing various machine learning algorithms such as Random Forest, Decision Tree, Gaussian Naive Bayes, K-Means Clustering, and K-Nearest Neighbors, the system initially assesses their accuracy in generating precise and individualized dietary recommendations. Subsequently, based on the evaluation, NutriWear selects K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) for its superior accuracy performance. By implementing KNN, the system ensures optimal health outcomes and addresses the challenges of obesity and sedentary lifestyles. Evaluation measures demonstrate the effectiveness of NutriWear in offering personalized dietary suggestions. In summary, NutriWear represents a notable advancement in personalized health management, providing practical strategies for enhancing health outcomes and addressing the challenges of obesity and sedentary lifestyles.

articleTitle: Unraveling IoT Network Security with Snort for Robust Intrusion Detection and Prevention
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has brought unprecedented connectivity, transforming technology across industries. This interconnected landscape, however, presents unprecedented network security challenges. This paper examines Snort's role as a powerful tool for Intrusion Detection in the network and the ways to prevent the intrusion detection and thoroughly investigates the security challenges posed by IoT networks. In light of the growing number of connected devices, the study focuses on specific vulnerabilities, emphasizing issues such as resource constraints, diverse communication protocols, and the need for tailored security measures. The paper provides a thorough examination of Snort's architecture and its application through the development of custom rules for detecting IoT threats. Practical implementation strategies such as network segmentation and continuous monitoring are investigated. The conclusion emphasizes how critical it is to understand threats unique to the Internet of Things and how to use Snort to fortify network defenses in this complex and ever-changing ecosystem.

articleTitle: Predictive Analytics for Early Electrical Fire Detection in IoT Networks Using Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Ensuring safety against potential fire threats is of utmost significance due to the development of IoT devices in numerous areas. Most of the time, human involvement is required for traditional fire detection systems, which lack proactive capabilities. This research presents a new technique for electrical fire detection in Internet of Things (IoT) networks using predictive analytics, utilizing the Random Forest algorithm. To proactively detect and reduce fire hazards before they become catastrophic by using the abundance of data produced by IoT sensors. Data such as current measurements, temperature, humidity, and other relevant features may be retrieved in real-time via IoT devices that are integrated into electrical systems according to the suggested system. Random Forest classifier is taught to interpret and classified patterns that suggest potential fire dangers using data preparation, feature engineering, and supervised learning methods. Standard validation measures are used to verify the model's performance, providing its dependability and robustness. IoT network infrastructure deployment of the trained model allows for early identification of possible fire hazards and continuous monitoring. The system's capabilities can be including more sensors and advanced machine learning algorithms. By automating the monitoring process and enabling early detection, the suggested solution increases efficiency and safer and more robust IoT environment.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of Artificial Intelligence for Enhancing Decision-Making Process of Recruitment in HRM Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into the recruitment process represents a significant advancement in Human Resource Management (HRM), aiming to optimize the efficiency and effectiveness of hiring practices. This paper explores the effectiveness of AI in improving decision-making processes within HRM, focusing on machine learning's role in streamlining candidate sourcing, enhancing candidate experience, boosting screening efficiency, optimizing interview processes, and improving onboarding experiences. By examining various studies and technological applications, it highlights the transformative potential of AI in recruitment, addressing challenges such as bias mitigation, engagement improvement, and access expansion to diverse talent pools. The research underscores the critical need for developing human-centric AI systems that prioritize transparency, privacy, accountability, fairness, and societal benefit. Through a comprehensive analysis, the paper advocates for the strategic implementation of AI in recruitment, emphasizing continuous monitoring, evaluation, and the necessary training for HR professionals to harness AI's full potential.

articleTitle: A PSO based Computation Offloading Model in Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Limitations of traditional cloud computing have fueled the rise of edge computing. This technique addresses the latency and real-time processing issues that come with using a typical cloud, and it operates at the edge of the network. While the applications of edge computing have grown, it's requiring a more sophisticated offloading strategy. Considerations needed to be made for elements including network circumstances, computing complexity, and energy efficiency. In this work, a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) based offloading model is proposed to optimize computation offloading in edge computing. PSO dynamically distributes the tasks for optimal efficiency and highlights its effectiveness in minimizing system costs, reducing task execution time and energy consumption, that improve overall performance.

articleTitle: An Elephant Identification Emissary: A Technological Odyssey in Elephant Recognition with IP & AI Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: With human-elephant conflicts escalating across Asia and Africa, innovative solutions are needed to identify and track individual elephants. An extensive elephant imagery dataset and advanced computer vision techniques are explored in this work for the automatic recognition of individual elephants using deep neural networks. More than 1000 images of elephants in varied natural environments were collected and processed to deal with variations in lighting, equipment, and pose. An evaluation of three convolutional neural network architectures for multi-class elephant recognition was conducted - SimCLR for self-supervised pretraining, LeNet-5, and Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Networks. With test images, the BRNN model correctly identified the elephant with 96.2% accuracy. Test results have a precision and recall of 95.5% and 96.9%, respectively. Results from these studies demonstrate the effectiveness of deep learning for elephant recognition, enabling enhanced monitoring, conservation, and conflict mitigation. However, challenges remain in model transparency, ethical implementation, integration with existing frameworks, etc. Using automated elephant identification technology, this work advances the co-existence of humans and elephants.

articleTitle: Genetic and Decision Tree-Based Secure Data Dissemination Framework for Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: In this article, we proposed a hybrid model comprising a genetic algorithm and a decision tree for secure data exchange in autonomous vehicles (AVs). The integration of a genetic algorithm enables systematic feature optimization, enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of classification models. Extensive performance assessments, including metrics such as receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and a convergence curve, substantiate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in addressing classification tasks. A robust model is presented that could thrive in the dynamic environment of AV, as a result of which the security and efficiency of the Intelligent Transportation Systems is further strengthened. We focus on the practical implications of our research, and consequently, the real-world applications relating to the evolving AV environment.

articleTitle: Neural Harmony: Advancing Composition with RNN-LSTM in Music Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: This research delves into the innovative realm of melody generation through neural networks, specifically focusing on the efficacy of Recurrent Neural Networks with Long Short-Term Memory (RNN-LSTM). Comprising three integral phases, our study commences with meticulous data preprocessing, emphasizing comprehensive preparation. This phase involves verifying acceptable durations, transposing melodies to fundamental keys, and encoding them into a timeseries- like representation. The diverse music dataset employed establishes a robust foundation for subsequent analysis and training. Building upon the solid groundwork of preprocessing, our approach advances to model development and training. Leveraging TensorFlow, we meticulously construct an RNNLSTM architecture tailored to capture intricate temporal dependencies and complex structural patterns inherent in melodies. The training process is a meticulous journey, involving compilation and iterative refinement, culminating in a robust framework poised for melody generation. In the final phase, our trained model ventures into the realm of creativity, generating melodies through innovative sampling techniques. The incorporation of temperature-based sampling adds a layer of sophistication, enabling our system to craft novel compositions while adhering to learned musical structures. This research serves as a pioneering contribution to music generation, seamlessly bridging theoretical music concepts, practical implementation in Python utilizing TensorFlow/Keras, and groundbreaking approaches to neural network-based melody creation. Notably, our findings underscore the transformative potential of RNN-LSTM architectures. These architectures prove adept at capturing and re-creating intricate musical nuances, thereby making significant strides in the everevolving landscape of artificial intelligence within the realm of creative arts.

articleTitle: Optimization of Hyperparameters on Migraine Classification Using Artificial Neural Networks on Human Brain's Neuronal Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: The complicated network arrangement of neurons and the information processing method seen in the human brain serve as a source of inspiration for artificial neural networks. In a manner that is analogous to this configuration, artificial neurons are structured into input, hidden, and output layers. This arrangement makes it easier for data to go through the network and be processed. While Back-propagation algorithms modify weights to minimize output errors using a variety of hyperparameters, Feed Forward propagation algorithms are responsible for driving input processing via hidden layers. Appropriate activation functions are very necessary in order to successfully capture complicated nonlinear mappings between layers. One of the most important aspects of the progress that has been made in research is the experimentation with various parameters in the training of artificial neural networks. For the purpose of this paper, artificial neural networks will be trained using a variety of parameters, such as activation functions, number of layers and nodes, epochs, optimizer, batch size, and loss functions, in order to investigate the influence that these parameters have on the classification of migraine kinds by utilizing a specific dataset. By conducting an analysis of these hyperparameters, the purpose of the research is to provide information that can be used to decide which parameter combinations are the most successful for improving the results of network training.

articleTitle: An Implementation of Interactive Mobile Development System using React Native and Firebase to Elevate Food Delivery Platform: Healfit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: The Healfit website is a dedicated platform that aims to change the way we think about healthy eating. This unique online service allows customers to order healthful meals from a broad menu from the comfort of their own homes. Healfit promotes well-being by offering a variety of nutritional options, catering to a wide range of dietary preferences, and encouraging a seamless user experience. It emphasizes the user-friendly interface, which makes food selection and ordering simple. Users may easily customize their meals to meet their nutritional needs, making it an excellent alternative for health-conscious people. The website's powerful search and filtering capabilities ensure that users can easily find meals that meet their dietary needs. Healfit prioritises openness by offering precise nutritional information for each menu item, allowing consumers to make educated decisions. The platform's dedication to user pleasure extends to its fast delivery services, which ensure that fresh and nutritious meals are delivered on time. The Healfit website, with an aim to promote healthier eating habits, has the potential to dramatically contribute to individuals' overall well-being. It not only makes ordering nutritious meals easier, but it also serves as a significant aid in choosing healthier food choices, leading to enhanced health and vigour.

articleTitle: Innovative Solutions for Cervical Cancer: Deep Learning Models for Accurate Stage Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Contemporary Computing and Communications (InC4)
abstract: Cervical cancer, caused by the skin infection of the Human papillomavirus (HPV), ranked as the fourth most prevalent cancer globally, has profound and sometimes fatal implications for women. With approximately 500,000 new cases reported annually, the disease significantly impacts women's overall well-being. Ongoing efforts by researchers focus on developing a more cost-effective solution than regular HPV testing to manage and control this widespread health concern. Our research included an innovative framework for identifying and classifying stages of cervical cancer by processing the images of the tumours. To optimize the performance of our model, we developed a unique approach for selecting the best image data points by calculating a score, which is defined as the product of focus, sharpness, and resolution. Additionally, our study distinguishes itself by integrating three diverse feature extraction techniques–Local Binary Pattern (LBP), ResNet, and VGGNet–an inclusive strategy not commonly observed in similar projects. We even added deep convolutional architectures and machine learning techniques, including Random Forest, SVM, Decision Tree, XGBoost, a basic Neural Network Classifier, and a Multi-layered Perceptron (MLP). This hybrid approach allowed for an intrinsic comparison, identifying the most effective strategy among these. In contrast to current state-of-the-art methods, our approach yielded around 75% accuracy and 81% AUC score, which is greater than the existing studies on such dataset.
